text:
Felix Schneider: working through the perf-canary dashboard + alert wiring. question for @Rafael Mendes / @Sean Gallagher: what’s the preferred format for the incident-bot post + PagerDuty event so the page includes runbook + dashboard links without being a wall of text?

Rafael Mendes: yep. for PD we should use:
- short `summary`
- consistent `dedup_key`
- put the rest in `custom_details`
incident-bot can render it nicer (fields + buttons).

Sean Gallagher: +1. also want the bot post to include “is this paging or ticket” signal. We’ll start paging only on sev2+ (once tuned). sev3 -> ticket.

Allison Grant: from obs-standards side: please keep field names stable (we’ll be parsing for dashboards + postmortems). also: avoid putting giant arrays in custom_details, PD truncates.

Felix Schneider: makes sense. what are we standardizing on for the “links”? like 1) grafana per-model view 2) runbook 3) deploy diff

Tomáš Novák: for responders, top 2 links should be:
1) runbook (triage checklist)
2) grafana “overview” for that model/region
then optionally “compare slices” + “recent deploys”.
If we only get 2, do those.

Caleb Johnson: + include trace search link if possible (even if it’s just a pre-filtered query). when people are digging into p95 jumps, they’ll want request-level samples.

Logan Wright: reminder: incident-bot payload should be < ~8KB if we want it to reliably post + not get truncated in the webhook path. better to link out than embed large context.

Nadia Rahman: re: what fields to include, please include the exact slice keys we’re alerting on:
- model
- region
- gpu_sku
- scheduler_mode
- runtime_build (or runtime_version)
- streaming (true/false)
so we can quickly confirm the metrics aggregation matches.

Thomas Baird: + dedup strategy matters here. we should dedup on *slice*, not just model. otherwise one noisy gpu sku pages repeatedly while masking another regression.
Proposed: `dedup_key = perf-canary|<metric>|<model>|<region>|<gpu_sku>|<scheduler_mode>|<streaming>`
NOT including runtime_build in dedup_key (so we don’t create a new incident every deploy).

Rafael Mendes: agree. PD dedup should stay stable across runtime_build. runtime_build should go in details + in the incident-bot message.

Felix Schneider: ok. incident-bot formatting: do we have a template we can copy? I can implement in perf-canary side but want to match other alert posts.

Rafael Mendes: here’s what we’ve been using in other services (pseudo), incident-bot supports a “fields” block:
```
summary: "Perf regression: p95 latency +18% (baseline 7d)"
severity: "critical" | "error" | "warning"
source: "perf-canary"
dedup_key: "perf-canary|p95_latency|llama-3.1-70b|us-east|h100|sched=v2|streaming=true"
custom_details:
  metric: "p95_latency_ms"
  regression_pct: "+18%"
  current_value: "412ms"
  baseline_value: "350ms"
  window: "10m"
  baseline_window: "7d median"
  model: "llama-3.1-70b"
  region: "us-east"
  gpu_sku: "h100"
  scheduler_mode: "v2_pinned"
  streaming: "true"
  runtime_build: "runtime-1.18.0-rc3"
  runtime_sha: "8b3f4a1"
  detector: "rolling_median_v1"
  min_samples: "120"
  canary_qps: "0.2"
links:
  grafana_overview: "https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/perf-canary/overview?model=..."
  grafana_slice: "https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/perf-canary/slice?..."
  runbook: "https://confluence.redwood.ai/x/perf-canary-runbook"
  deploys: "https://console.redwood.ai/deploys?service=runtime&region=us-east"
  traces: "https://trace.redwood.ai/search?service=runtime&tag=source:perf-canary..."
```
We can drop some fields if too long.

Allison Grant: minor: please use `p95_latency_ms` and `tokens_per_sec` as canonical metric names (per spec). avoid “tok/s” / “tps” variations in payload.

Sean Gallagher: also, include “action” hint in the message text:
- “If during deploy window: likely expected, check suppression”
- “If outside deploy window: consider rollback / pin scheduler / disable experimental heuristic X”
Not too verbose, just 2 bullets.

Tomáš Novák: +1. runbook has the full checklist, but having “what to do first” in the page helps.

Felix Schneider: for incident-bot post, something like:
- first line summary
- then a compact block of key/value fields
- then links
- then 2 bullets for actions
Ok?

Rafael Mendes: yep. and please tag the routing in the bot message:
- `Oncall: SRE` initially
- when confirmed, bot can open a Linear task + @mention runtime-oncall (manual for now is fine).

incident-bot: (test message)
Perf regression: p95_latency_ms +18% vs 7d median
Slice: model=llama-3.1-70b region=us-east gpu_sku=h100 scheduler_mode=v2_pinned streaming=true
Runtime: runtime-1.18.0-rc3 (8b3f4a1)
Links: Grafana overview • Slice drilldown • Runbook • Recent deploys
Actions: Check deploy annotations + suppression window; if correlated w/ runtime deploy, consider rollback to last known-good.

Logan Wright: looks good. one more thing: don’t include per-request IDs in the alert payload (privacy + cardinality). trace link is enough.

Nadia Rahman: can we ensure the “Slice:” line order stays consistent? makes copy/paste into queries easier.

Thomas Baird: +1. also, don’t add new dimensions later without checking dedup/PD incident count impact.

Felix Schneider: ack. I’ll update the dashboard panels to include a “Copy slice query” helper and will mirror the same field order in the bot.

Sean Gallagher: cool. once we have first week of data, we’ll revisit severity mapping + whether we start ticket-first for sev3.

Rafael Mendes: follow-up: I’ll add this template to the alert-routing doc and make sure the PD service expects `source=perf-canary` events. (ENG-2848)

Allison Grant: please link the metric spec in the runbook too (responders keep asking “how is p95 computed”).

Tomáš Novák: done, I’ll update runbook section “Understanding the signal” + add the grafana links list.

Felix Schneider: perfect, thanks all.
